# v2.57-dev Release Notes

## Fixed: the company-scoped Offerings migration (v2.56) failed to apply

The database migration shipped in **v2.56-dev** could not be applied — it tried
to drop the offering-name unique index before dropping the two foreign keys that
depend on it, so PostgreSQL rejected it (`cannot drop index offerings_name_key
because other objects depend on it`) and the update rolled back. The migration
now drops those child foreign keys first, so it applies cleanly. It has been
tested end-to-end on both an empty database and a populated one (existing
offerings are reassigned to the oldest company, and their specialisation and
requirement rows are preserved).

### If your v2.56 update already failed and rolled back

Your data is safe — the failed migration rolls back atomically, so you're still
on your previous version. But PostgreSQL has recorded the migration as *failed*,
which blocks any further migration until it's cleared. Before updating to v2.57,
run this once from the app directory (e.g. `/opt/training-tracker`) so the fixed
migration can re-apply from scratch:

```bash
npx prisma migrate resolve --rolled-back 20260721000000_company_scoped_offerings
```

Then run the update as usual. (If your v2.56 update never ran or never reached
the migration step, no action is needed — just update.)

### Notes

- No schema or feature changes versus v2.56 — this is purely the corrected
  migration for the company-scoped Offerings feature.
